tasks.short: Check payment requests and approve spending within my mandate.

today.trigger: A payment request or AFAS approval batch arrives.
steps: Read the request and supporting invoice or contract.
Check budget, coding, duplicate payments and supplier details.
Ask the requester or bookkeeper to resolve missing information.
Approve within mandate or refer to the Finance Director.
Record the decision for payment preparation and audit.
drudgery: Opening several screens to check one request
Repeating checks already performed by the bookkeeper
today.time_sinks: Assumed main delays are incomplete requests and scattered evidence; bank release is a separate control.

lenses.faster: Document searches and repeat checks disappear into a single evidence pack. An illustrative 60-minute batch becomes 30 minutes: 10 checking evidence, 12 resolving exceptions and eight approving.
lenses.autonomous: An AFAS request starts fixed checks against budget, contract, duplicate and mandate rules. The controller approves each complete request within mandate; changed IBANs require independent verification before payment.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give site managers a purchase commitment check before they place urgent orders. Demand would grow if this became cheap and quick enough for routine operational purchases.
lenses.joy: I would lose the screen switching and repeated document chasing. I would spend more time challenging avoidable spending and helping sites buy sensibly.
lenses.options: Show approve now, stage the purchase or defer it, with cash and operational consequences. Those alternatives can change the spending decision when a request is affordable but poorly timed.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward unusual commitments and recurring control failures. With delegated authority to resolve defined budget exceptions, the role becomes more expert in commercial judgement.
reach: Absorb the Bookkeeper's task of assembling payment approval evidence; learn AFAS workflow configuration and supplier master controls.

tasks.human_edge: I recognise commercial pressure, suspicious urgency and relationships that make a formally correct request questionable; I remain accountable for approval within my mandate.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: budget limits, duplicate tests, required documents and mandates can be written as rules; a model is unnecessary for the approval checks.

in_practice.trigger: A request enters the AFAS approval workflow.
steps: Read request fields, supporting documents and the current approval matrix through approved access.
Run fixed checks and build a linked evidence pack.
Route missing information to the requester and flag duplicates or changed bank details.
Present a recommendation to the authorised approver.
Record approval and pass the request into the existing payment process.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller or Finance Director approves each request according to mandate; authorised bank signers separately release the payment batch.
systems: Proposed rules service and approval queue
data_needed: Requests, invoices and purchase commitments
Budgets and contracts
Supplier master changes and prior payments
Approval limits and bank signing mandates
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS approval history, with rule results and evidence references retained in an access-controlled SharePoint register.

evidence.claim: Fixed financial matching rules are already used in AFAS, although its bank matching page does not prove the proposed disbursement workflow.
The proposed checks and 50% saving are planning assumptions requiring validation against existing AFAS automation.

risks: A compromised supplier change passes otherwise valid checks.
Existing AFAS controls already perform much of the proposed work, reducing incremental savings.
Combining request preparation, approval and bank release weakens segregation of duties.
research_questions: Which checks does AFAS already perform, and how many controller minutes remain per request?
Can supporting contracts, budgets and supplier changes be accessed reliably without broad write permissions?
What proportion of requests need commercial judgement or missing evidence?
Can the approval pack preserve separate requester, approver and bank signer identities?

tasks.short: Check cash, reserves and financial obligations, and flag anything that needs action.

today.trigger: The daily cash review starts or a material financial event occurs.
steps: Collect bank balances, open receivables, payables and payroll commitments.
Reconcile balances and identify stale or missing transactions.
Update expected cash movements and reserve headroom.
Check applicable tax deadlines, financing conditions and internal limits.
Discuss exceptions and document the required action.
drudgery: Reconciling reports with different cut-off times
today.time_sinks: Assumed main effort is establishing a trustworthy cash position; the nightly Power BI extract cannot establish intraday liquidity.

lenses.faster: Scheduled imports, reconciliation and limit checks replace spreadsheet assembly. An illustrative 60-minute review becomes 27 minutes: seven checking freshness, 12 investigating exceptions and eight accepting the assessment and assigning actions.
lenses.autonomous: A new bank statement or scheduled daily run refreshes the cash position and flags breached limits. I approve the daily assessment before it supports cash decisions; the workflow does not move money.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: assess payroll-week liquidity headroom every working day during seasonal peaks. Demand would grow as cheaper checks let operations test late customer receipts and flex staffing commitments sooner.
lenses.joy: I would stop rebuilding yesterday's cash spreadsheet. I would spend more time explaining emerging shortages and agreeing practical responses.
lenses.options: Compare on-time collections, delayed receipts and a seasonal staffing surge against the same cash floor. This can change when we escalate a funding need or challenge a spending commitment.
lenses.altitude: My week centres on early interventions rather than balance collection. Delegated authority to require recovery plans for cash-limit exceptions would make the role more expert in liquidity control.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's routine short-term cash bridge preparation; learn cash forecast drivers and financing covenant definitions.

tasks.human_edge: I judge whether customer promises, operational commitments and financing conditions are credible, and whether an apparent breach needs escalation despite a technically balanced report.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: balance reconciliation, dated cash movements, deadlines and documented limits are repeatable calculations; judgement stays in exception resolution.

in_practice.trigger: A daily schedule runs after bank and AFAS data are available, with extra runs for material events.
steps: Import bank and ledger data and display their cut-off times.
Reconcile balances and stop the assessment if critical inputs are missing.
Calculate cash headroom and test documented obligations and limits.
Present exceptions, assumptions and responsible owners to the controller.
Record the accepted assessment and follow up agreed actions.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller accepts the daily assessment and decides escalation; the Finance Director retains financing and cash allocation authority.
data_needed: Bank statements and balances with timestamps
Open receivables, payables and scheduled payments
Aggregate payroll and agency payment commitments
Financing terms, applicable deadlines and approved cash floors
in_practice.logs_to: A dated SharePoint cash-control register containing source cut-offs, reconciliation results, exceptions and controller acceptance.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports rule-based bank statement matching using financial identifiers.
Financial agent governance guidance calls for mandatory human approval of cash allocation and timestamped logs.
The monitoring design and estimated saving are untested at Noordhaven.

risks: Stale data creates false liquidity headroom.
Undocumented commitments or financing terms escape the checks.
A clean dashboard is mistaken for proof of complete legal compliance.
research_questions: How quickly can bank and AFAS data be obtained, and where do cut-offs differ?
Which legal, contractual and internal limits actually apply to Noordhaven?
How often do unrecorded commitments materially change the cash position?
Would daily reconciled monitoring identify problems earlier than the current process?

tasks.short: Recommend when we need funding and what to do with spare cash.

today.trigger: A cash forecast, investment request or financing review indicates a shortage or surplus.
steps: Review cash forecasts, seasonal working capital and planned investments.
Collect financing terms and permitted surplus investment options.
Model funding needs, costs and downside headroom.
Discuss operational assumptions with sites and FP&A.
Recommend an option to the Finance Director.
drudgery: Copying terms between documents and spreadsheets
today.time_sinks: Assumed main effort is scenario preparation and validating uncertain receipts, staffing costs and investment timing.

lenses.faster: A copilot prepares comparable scenarios and a sourced first draft of the recommendation. An illustrative 120-minute analysis becomes 84 minutes: 24 validating assumptions, 35 judging options and 25 discussing and finalising the recommendation.
lenses.autonomous: A projected cash-floor breach or material surplus prompts a draft analysis using approved models. I choose assumptions and make the recommendation; the Finance Director approves funding or investment action.
lenses.ambitious: New service: provide the Rotterdam site manager with a funding assessment before seasonal capacity commitments are made. Demand would grow if these assessments became quick enough to inform operational planning.
lenses.joy: I would lose repetitive scenario setup and presentation formatting. I would gain time to test whether the business really needs the funding and negotiate better timing.
lenses.options: Compare borrowing, releasing working capital and staging capital expenditure under delayed-receipt scenarios. These alternatives can change whether we seek funds at all, rather than merely which lender we choose.
lenses.altitude: My week includes more working-capital discussions before commitments are signed. With authority to require a downside funding case for major proposals, the job becomes more expert in capital allocation.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's first-pass funding sensitivity analysis; learn debt pricing, covenant headroom and treasury policy.

tasks.human_edge: I weigh business resilience, bank relationships and operational consequences that cannot be inferred reliably from forecast numbers alone.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the useful work is exploring assumptions and trade-offs with management; calculations can be deterministic while a model helps prepare and challenge the analysis.

in_practice.trigger: The controller opens a funding review after a forecast threshold or investment proposal is flagged.
steps: Load the reconciled cash forecast, approved financing terms and investment proposal.
Ask the copilot to identify missing assumptions and draft alternative funding paths.
Calculate scenarios in a controlled spreadsheet with visible formulas.
Challenge downside cases and validate operational assumptions with owners.
Submit a sourced recommendation to the Finance Director.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller owns the recommendation; authorised management approves financing, surplus investment and any bank instruction.
data_needed: Reconciled cash forecast and forecast errors
Financing agreements, fees and covenant definitions
Treasury policy and permitted instruments
Investment timing and operational dependencies
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint funding decision file containing model version, source terms, assumptions, AI draft and final recommendation.

evidence.claim: Governance guidance supports retaining human approval for cash allocation.
Scenario preparation can be assisted, but the proposed funding workflow and 30% saving have no direct case in the supplied digest.

risks: Plausible scenarios conceal unrealistic collection or operating assumptions.
The model misreads financing restrictions or compares unavailable products.
A recommendation confuses forecast surplus with cash available for investment.
research_questions: How much current analysis time goes into preparation versus judgement and negotiation?
Are financing terms and permitted investments documented clearly enough to model?
Would alternative scenarios have changed any recent funding recommendation?
Does FP&A already provide this analysis, leaving little work for the controller to absorb?

tasks.short: Coordinate budgets and financial plans across the three sites.

today.trigger: A budget cycle, reforecast or significant procurement or investment decision starts.
steps: Set planning assumptions, deadlines and responsibilities with Finance leadership.
Collect site plans and FP&A submissions.
Reconcile versions and challenge inconsistent drivers.
Discuss trade-offs with site managers and budget owners.
Consolidate recommendations and track agreed actions.
today.time_sinks: Assumed main delays are late submissions, incompatible assumptions and repeated agreement on ownership.

lenses.faster: Version comparisons, missing-input lists and meeting briefs are prepared automatically. An illustrative 120-minute coordination cycle becomes 90 minutes: 20 checking submissions, 45 resolving trade-offs and 25 agreeing actions.
lenses.autonomous: A planning milestone starts completeness and consistency checks and produces a draft discussion pack. I lead the discussions and approve priorities, responsibilities and escalations within my mandate.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: rebalance site spending priorities monthly when volumes change, rather than waiting for the annual budget cycle. Demand would grow if preparing a reliable decision pack became cheaper.
lenses.joy: I would lose version chasing and meeting administration. I would spend more time getting site managers to agree on realistic plans.
lenses.options: Compare protecting service capacity, cutting discretionary spending and staging investments across the three sites. Seeing the combined effects can change which site receives scarce budget.
lenses.altitude: My week moves toward cross-site trade-offs and delivery follow-up. Delegated authority to reject inconsistent submissions and convene budget owners makes the role more expert in operational planning.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's planning submission coordination and first consistency review; learn operational drivers and planning model ownership.

tasks.human_edge: I resolve competing interests, understand why managers resist a target and secure commitments they will actually deliver.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: preparation is repeatable, but directing people and settling priorities require the controller to lead.

in_practice.trigger: An approved budget or reforecast milestone becomes due.
steps: Collect versioned submissions and the approved assumptions.
Run fixed checks for missing inputs, inconsistent drivers and reconciliation differences.
Draft a briefing with unresolved choices and proposed discussion questions.
Have the controller lead the planning discussion and confirm decisions.
Publish the approved plan and action register through the existing process.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves the discussion pack and action record; the Finance Director and budget owners approve plans under existing mandates.
data_needed: Planning calendar and submission owners
Site volumes, staffing plans and spending proposals
Approved assumptions and budget limits
Prior decisions and unresolved actions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint planning folder with submission versions, check results, approved decisions and named action owners.

evidence.claim: A copilot can compare planning submissions and draft briefs, but the supplied digest does not document a comparable coordination case.
The 25% saving assumes preparation falls while management discussion and agreement remain substantial.

risks: Automatically consolidated plans hide inconsistent site assumptions.
Draft action records imply agreement that participants never gave.
Financial planning bypasses HR and OR involvement where proposed workforce changes require it.
research_questions: What share of coordination time is administration rather than negotiation?
Do all three sites use compatible drivers and planning templates?
Which decisions may the controller make, and which require Finance Director approval?
Can the pilot reduce planning rework without duplicating FP&A responsibilities?

tasks.short: Advise management on financial priorities and the actions worth taking.

today.trigger: Management requests advice or financial results reveal a material opportunity or problem.
steps: Clarify the decision, time horizon and management objectives.
Gather financial and operational evidence.
Test causes, alternatives and consequences.
Discuss the recommendation with relevant managers.
Record the decision and review its outcome.
drudgery: Finding the assumptions behind earlier decisions
today.time_sinks: Assumed main effort is distinguishing a real business issue from a reporting effect and securing a decision management will support.

lenses.faster: A copilot assembles sourced evidence and drafts alternative recommendations and objections. An illustrative 120-minute advice cycle becomes 90 minutes: 20 checking evidence, 40 forming judgement and 30 discussing and finalising advice.
lenses.autonomous: A management question or controller-selected variance starts a draft analysis. I frame the question, verify the reasoning and give the advice; management makes the decision.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give the Venlo site manager a monthly customer-margin decision clinic. Demand would grow if preparation became cheap enough to examine pricing and service choices before margins deteriorate.
lenses.joy: I would lose the repetitive background slides. I would gain more time for candid conversations about which actions management should stop or start.
lenses.options: Compare repricing, changing service conditions and improving warehouse productivity for a weak customer account. Different combinations can change the recommendation from cost reduction to a commercial renegotiation.
lenses.altitude: My week contains more decision discussions and follow-up on whether advice worked. A formal right to bring material margin issues onto the management agenda would make the role more expert and influential.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's initial variance narrative and option paper; learn customer profitability, operational costing and how to evaluate causal claims.

tasks.human_edge: I understand management's real constraints, challenge convenient explanations and take responsibility for advice that affects relationships and operating choices.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the decision question and interpretation evolve through discussion, and the controller must lead rather than approve a finished machine recommendation.

in_practice.trigger: The controller accepts a management question or selects a material issue for investigation.
steps: Define the decision, relevant evidence and criteria for success.
Retrieve authorised financial and operational information with source references.
Generate competing explanations and calculate their implications in a controlled model.
Challenge the alternatives with relevant managers and select a recommendation.
Record the decision, assumptions and date for outcome review.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller signs off the advice and its evidence; management approves the business action.
data_needed: Validated financial results and operational drivers
Customer or service profitability where available
Management objectives and decision constraints
Previous recommendations and actual outcomes
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint management decision register with evidence, scenario model, final advice and subsequent outcome.

evidence.claim: The supplied close benchmark explicitly excludes client communication, asking the right questions and tacit context; it does not establish autonomous management advice.
The proposed advice workflow and saving are planning estimates.

risks: A convincing narrative confuses correlation with causation.
Incomplete cost allocation produces misleading customer margins.
Management treats multiple generated scenarios as independent evidence.
research_questions: Which recurring management questions consume the most preparation time?
Are operational drivers and cost allocations reliable enough to support the proposed advice?
Would alternative recommendations have changed recent management decisions?
Can outcomes be tracked well enough to distinguish useful advice from persuasive writing?

tasks.short: Check the costs and financial risks of employee benefits and insurance.

today.trigger: An insurance renewal, benefits budget review or relevant rule change occurs.
steps: Collect policies, renewal terms and aggregate workforce information.
Review financial implications with HR, Compensation and Benefits, Payroll and the broker.
Compare premiums, coverage, exclusions and employer exposure.
Update benefit and insurance budgets.
Recommend financial actions and record the agreed responsibilities.
drudgery: Reconciling different headcount and payroll bases
today.time_sinks: Assumed controller scope is financial oversight; HR and specialists retain benefits administration, individual cases and Dutch employment-law interpretation.

lenses.faster: One model step produces a cited comparison of renewal documents; fixed calculations build the budget. An illustrative 120-minute review becomes 78 minutes: 23 checking clauses, 25 validating costs and 30 agreeing the recommendation with specialists.
lenses.autonomous: A renewal document or relevant change notice starts a draft comparison and cost-impact worksheet. HR, the broker and I validate the interpretation before any benefits or insurance decision.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give the Compensation and Benefits Specialist a quarterly site-level view of insured and retained absence costs. Demand would grow if preparing an aggregate view became inexpensive.
lenses.joy: I would lose repeated policy-table comparisons. I would spend more time deciding whether apparent premium savings expose the business to unacceptable risk.
lenses.options: Compare higher deductibles, different coverage limits and the current policy using the same exposure assumptions. This can change the chosen balance between premium cost and retained risk.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward understanding total employer exposure rather than assembling premiums. Authority to require a financial risk assessment before renewal would make the role more expert without transferring HR's benefits decisions.
reach: Absorb the Compensation and Benefits Specialist's financial comparison of renewal options; learn Dutch absence insurance, WIA/WGA exposure, pension costs and applicable CAO provisions.

tasks.human_edge: I judge whether coverage fits Noordhaven's operational risks and recognise when employee consequences or ambiguous exclusions require HR, legal or broker expertise.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: a fixed renewal workflow needs one cited extraction and comparison of messy policy text, followed by deterministic cost calculations and specialist review.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised user adds a renewal pack or relevant change notice to SharePoint.
steps: Collect current and proposed terms plus aggregate exposure data.
Extract a cited comparison of premiums, limits, exclusions and changed wording.
Calculate budget and retained-risk scenarios in a controlled spreadsheet.
Have the controller, HR and broker resolve material uncertainties.
Record the recommendation and route the approved decision through the existing process.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller validates financial effects; HR and relevant specialists validate employment implications, with OR involvement where applicable and management approval before commitment.
data_needed: Current and proposed policies and broker explanations
Aggregate headcount, payroll and insured exposure
Relevant CAO and benefits provisions
Aggregate claims and absence-cost history without diagnoses
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint renewal file with cited clauses, calculation versions, specialist comments and approvals.

evidence.claim: Cited document comparison can support benefits financial reviews, but the supplied digest contains no directly comparable insurance implementation.
Dutch benefits and absence arrangements require local interpretation; US workers' compensation assumptions should not be imported into this workflow.

risks: A summary misses an exclusion that changes the real value of coverage.
Medical or identifiable absence information enters a finance AI workspace contrary to AVG access limits.
Advice confuses insurance coverage with employer duties under the Wet verbetering poortwachter or applicable CAO.
research_questions: Which insurance and benefits activities actually belong to this controller rather than HR or the broker?
Can the financial comparison use aggregate data without individual health information?
Does a cited extraction reliably capture exclusions and changed terms in historical renewals?
Are quarterly site exposure views useful enough to influence renewal or prevention decisions?

tasks.short: Check that payroll deductions reconcile and reach the right ledger accounts.

today.trigger: The Payroll Specialist produces a payroll trial run or correction run.
steps: Obtain deduction totals, payroll control reports and the proposed journal.
Compare deductions against prior periods and approved rule changes.
Reconcile payroll, liability accounts and payment totals.
Investigate differences with the Payroll Specialist.
Approve the financial control result and retain evidence.
systems: AFAS Profit payroll and general ledger
drudgery: Copying payroll totals into reconciliation sheets
today.time_sinks: Assumed controller effort is deduction control and accounting, since AFAS calculates payroll and the Payroll Specialist owns payroll execution.

lenses.faster: Scheduled control reports and rule-based reconciliations replace manual copying and repeat calculations. An illustrative 60-minute check becomes 33 minutes: eight validating the run, 17 investigating exceptions and eight approving the control result.
lenses.autonomous: A payroll trial-run identifier starts reconciliations and approved variance tests. The Payroll Specialist resolves payroll issues, and I approve the financial reconciliation before the existing release gates.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give Payroll and the Tilburg site planner an early deduction-control check before peak-season payroll cut-off. Demand would grow if repeat checks became cheap enough to catch errors before the final run.
lenses.joy: I would lose repetitive spreadsheet tie-outs. I would spend more time preventing recurring payroll-control failures with the Payroll Specialist.
lenses.options: Compare a proposed deduction-rule correction in a sandbox against the current run, showing net-pay and liability effects. This can change whether Payroll corrects the current run or uses a permitted later correction.
lenses.altitude: My week centres on exception causes and payroll-to-ledger integrity. Delegated authority to hold financial sign-off on an unreconciled run makes the role more expert in controls, while Payroll retains technical payroll ownership.
reach: Absorb the Payroll Specialist's preparation of payroll-to-ledger control totals; learn AFAS payroll reporting, deduction categories and the two applicable CAO scopes.

tasks.human_edge: I distinguish a harmless timing difference from a payroll error affecting employees and ensure disputed deductions reach the Payroll Specialist rather than being accepted because totals balance.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: AFAS already calculates deductions; the additional value is reproducible reconciliation and exception detection, not model-generated payroll arithmetic.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS marks a payroll trial run ready for financial control.
steps: Read run-specific deduction totals, journal lines and approved control parameters.
Reconcile payroll liabilities, ledger mappings and payment totals.
Flag unexplained movements and differences without changing employee deductions.
Have Payroll resolve exceptions and rerun controls against the revised run identifier.
Capture controller sign-off before existing payroll and payment approvals.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves the reconciliation for the exact run; the Payroll Specialist authorises payroll changes and existing authorised signers release payments.
data_needed: Payroll run identifiers and deduction control totals
Payroll journals and liability account balances
Approved deduction rules, effective dates and ledger mappings
Prior-run comparisons and authorised corrections
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS run references and a restricted SharePoint reconciliation record containing checks, exceptions, resolutions and approvals.

evidence.claim: AFAS payroll is part of the supplied company system; deterministic reconciliation can extend its controls without using a model to calculate deductions.
The 45% saving concerns controller review effort and depends on controls not already being automated.

risks: A balanced journal contains an incorrect deduction or wrong employee treatment.
Approval applies to a superseded payroll run.
Payroll details are exposed beyond need-to-know access under AVG.
A finance control expands into employee scoring or employment decisions, requiring a separate assessment of EU AI Act applicability.
research_questions: Which deduction controls already run automatically in AFAS?
Can reports and approvals be bound reliably to an immutable payroll run identifier?
Which errors escape totals-based checks and need employee-level review by Payroll?
Can aggregate controls achieve the saving without expanding finance access to personal payroll data?

tasks.short: Deliver reconciled financial reports, forecasts and budgets that management can trust.

today.trigger: A month-end, forecast, budget or statutory reporting deadline approaches.
steps: Coordinate ledger close inputs and reconcile key balances.
Review accruals, reclassifications and unresolved accounting questions.
Consolidate financial statements, forecasts and budget outputs.
Investigate variances and draft explanations.
Review with the Finance Director and prepare approved reporting or filing outputs.
systems: External accountant or filing provider where required
today.time_sinks: Assumed main effort is resolving late evidence and accounting judgements; report preparation alone does not determine the close date.

lenses.faster: A model drafts supported accrual proposals and variance commentary while fixed queries build and reconcile tables. An illustrative 120-minute reporting cycle becomes 66 minutes: 16 validating sources, 30 reviewing accounting and forecast judgements and 20 approving the pack.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled close snapshot starts report assembly and one structured drafting step. I approve each journal proposal and the final pack after deterministic tie-outs; statutory submissions retain separate authorised approval.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give all three site managers a provisional margin and labour-cost pack before the final close. Demand would grow if inexpensive preparation made early corrective discussions practical, with uncertainty clearly marked.
lenses.joy: I would lose roll-forward work and repetitive commentary. I would spend more time resolving judgement calls and helping managers understand what changed.
lenses.options: Compare supported accrual ranges and alternative forecast drivers, keeping booked results separate from scenarios. This can change the forecast recommendation or trigger an additional evidence request before booking.
lenses.altitude: My week moves toward early accounting decisions, forecast challenge and review of recurring estimation errors. Delegated authority to reject unsupported submissions and enforce close readiness makes the role more expert in Dutch reporting and financial control.
reach: Absorb the Accountant's recurring accrual proposal preparation; learn the underlying evidence and Dutch GAAP treatment.
Absorb the FP&A Analyst's first variance commentary draft; learn site volume, productivity and labour-cost drivers.

tasks.human_edge: I decide whether evidence supports recognition, estimates and disclosures under Dutch GAAP, challenge operational explanations and stand behind the report with management and the auditor.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: a fixed workflow turns a defined evidence pack into checkable journal proposals and commentary; deterministic calculations and tie-outs control the numbers.

in_practice.trigger: A versioned AFAS close snapshot and required supporting schedules become available.
steps: Validate snapshot completeness and reconcile bank, receivables, payables and relevant subledgers to the general ledger.
Assemble report tables and approved forecast calculations using fixed queries and formulas.
Run one structured model step to draft cited accrual proposals and variance commentary.
Have the controller approve, adjust or reject proposals and resolve accounting questions.
Post approved journals through existing controls, rerun affected tie-outs and route the final pack for approval.
in_practice.human_gate: No proposed journal posts without authorised review; unexplained reconciliation differences block finalisation, and the Finance Director approves the final pack and relevant filing route.
systems: Proposed controlled extraction and reconciliation workflow
Power BI with explicit snapshot dates
External SBR filing solution if required
data_needed: Versioned trial balance and subledger reconciliations
Accrual handbook, materiality policy and prior estimates
Invoices, contracts and agency-hours evidence
Approved forecast and budget drivers
Applicable Dutch GAAP policies and statutory reporting requirements
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint close file retaining source snapshots, prompts, model version, drafts, reviewer decisions, AFAS journal identifiers and final tie-out results.

evidence.claim: Trintech offers accrual generation and roll-forward with review, approval and audit retention; this does not establish AFAS integration.
A field study reported a 7.5-day faster close among 79 small and mid-sized firms; it does not establish this task's saving at Noordhaven.
evidence.source: CFO Dive on Choi and Xie: https://www.cfodive.com/news/ai-cuts-monthly-financial-close-time-75-days-mit-stanford-study-accounting-accountants/757610/

evidence.claim: A vendor close benchmark reports substantial unsolved work and identifies accounting judgement as a bottleneck; its US GAAP setting limits transfer to Dutch reporting.
AFAS documents a separate reporting limitation for large-company filing; Noordhaven's classification and SBR route must be established.

risks: A plausible accrual or explanation lacks sufficient supporting evidence.
US GAAP benchmark results are treated as proof of Dutch GAAP or statutory filing competence.
A proposed journal changes balances after the reconciliations were approved.
Late staffing-agency invoices or unreliable hours data still determine the close date.
Forecast commentary hides uncertain operational assumptions.
research_questions: Which reporting steps actually lie on Noordhaven's close critical path?
Can historical Dutch GAAP accruals and commentary be reproduced with evidence the auditor accepts?
Can the workflow rerun tie-outs after every approved adjustment and retain a complete review trail?
What is Noordhaven's statutory size classification, and which provider handles any required SBR filing?

role.altitude: The controller becomes the person who makes the close and forecast dependable: resolving accounting judgements early, challenging site assumptions and turning exceptions into management decisions. Subject to Finance Director delegation, the role gains authority to hold unreconciled outputs, reject unsupported submissions and require recovery plans for material financial exceptions.
reach: Accountant: prepare recurring accrual proposals and supporting evidence, with stronger Dutch GAAP knowledge.
Bookkeeper: assemble payment approval evidence, with AFAS workflow and supplier-control skills.
FP&A Analyst: prepare initial cash scenarios, planning consistency checks and variance commentary, with operational modelling skills.
Payroll Specialist: prepare payroll-to-ledger control totals, with payroll reporting and CAO knowledge.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: prepare financial insurance comparisons, with Dutch employer-risk and policy interpretation skills.
role.ceiling_note: Current workflows, anatomy percentages and savings are planning assumptions, not observed measurements. The eight tasks cover about 725 of roughly 1,600 annual role hours; the proposed savings total about 294 hours, or 18% of the whole role, before any reinvestment or absorbed adjacent work. They release capacity rather than establish a headcount reduction, and they do not by themselves predict fewer days to close.
skills_to_grow: AFAS data access, workflow configuration and run-specific control design
SQL, controlled Excel models and reproducible reconciliations
Dutch GAAP, accrual evidence and statutory filing requirements
Cash forecasting, covenant interpretation and downside analysis
Warehouse, transport and flex-labour cost drivers
AI output evaluation, source checking and audit-trail retention
AVG access minimisation and recognising when employee-related AI needs separate EU AI Act assessment
Management challenge, negotiation and clear financial advice
role.ambitious_version: Run an earlier, evidence-backed close alongside a rolling site-level outlook that management uses to act before month-end. Use released capacity for provisional site margin discussions, seasonal liquidity warnings and follow-up on forecast errors; judge success by days to close, forecast accuracy and audit adjustments, while tracking effects on DSO and invoice touch rates separately.
